correctness.rationale: For a connected simple d-regular G (n≥3,d≥2), the Minkowski sum support h_K(u)=Σ_edges sqrt(u_i²+u_j²). For unit u put z_i=u_i². Since each edge sum z_i+z_j≤1, sqrt(s)≥s gives h_K(u)≥Σ_i degree(i)z_i=d, equality only for signed coordinate basis when connected degree≥2 (any distributed positive z creates an incident edge with 0<s<1). Thus dB_n is inscribed and contacts exactly ±d e_i. Coordinate support inequalities constrain each row norm of any inscribed ellipsoid affine map ≤d, so Hadamard proves unique John ball and unique centered maximal inball. Cauchy–Schwarz gives h²≤|E|Σ_edges(z_i+z_j)=n d²/2. Equality iff z_i+z_j=2/n along every edge; odd cycle forces all z_i=1/n, whereas connected bipartite graph forces one constant on each part and normalized a+b=2/n. Equality support points are Ru, giving 2^n sign points for nonbipartite, versus independent sign choices and a quarter-great-circle parameter for bipartite equal partitions p=n/2; interiors disjoint, endpoint identifications yield K_(2^p,2^p), cycle rank (2^p-1)^2. Independently derive Löwner optimality from signed flat contact design with E xx^T=(d²/2)I and tr(Q^-1)≤2/d², then AM–GM implies det Q≥(nd²/2)^n with equality only centered sphere. Independent checks on C3 and C4 reproduce h extrema and contacts. Finite checks do not substitute for all-graph proof.

evidence: Contact-locus topology K_(2^p,2^p) with first Betti (2^p−1)^2 is controlled solely by bipartiteness and n.
Ellipsoid identities hold with no vertex-transitivity hypothesis and have explicit extremizer certificates.
value.rationale: A sharp natural graph-geometric dictionary: without vertex transitivity both optimal Euclidean extremal ellipsoids become spheres with explicit radii, and bipartiteness determines whether the entire outer-contact set is discrete or a high-cycle-rank embedded complete bipartite graph. This is an exact classification for all connected regular graphs, not arbitrary small-parameter computation. The Betti number gives a motivated global topological invariant, potentially useful in discotope geometry and symmetric convexity.
residual_risks: Specializes to regular graphs and Euclidean metric; no general graph/polytope invariant extrapolation claimed.
